# Relay stage 3: Diagnose
Task: 00-restart-between-tasks-run-protocol
Working directory: /Volumes/Tera/dev/visual-relay
Protected paths (queue bookkeeping — never part of this task's diff): llm-tasks/, .relay/, .relay-scratch/, .swival/

## Task input
## Task: Add a "Restart Between Tasks" Run All protocol that relaunches the app after each task

Visual Relay is developed with Visual Relay: a queue of compounding tasks is
run against this repo, where each task's fix only helps the NEXT task if the
app is rebuilt and relaunched between them. Today a drain runs the same binary
end-to-end — the 2026-07-15 drain log shows every task executing under
`version=0.76+cfcc78d…` even as those very tasks sealed newer commits, so
fixes landed mid-drain were never live for the tasks that followed. Add a
third Run All protocol, **Restart Between Tasks**: identical to Sequential,
except that after a task seals its commit the app persists a handoff, quits,
relaunches itself (which recompiles from source), reopens the same repo, and
continues the queue where it left off.

### Current mechanics (verified)

- `RunAllMode` enum (`src/VisualRelay.Core/Queue/RunAllMode.cs`) has
  `Standard` and `Sequential`; the dropdown options come from
  `MainWindowViewModel.Properties.cs:12` and render in
  `src/VisualRelay.App/Views/Controls/TopBar.axaml:124` (a plain ComboBox with
  a tooltip describing the two modes).
- `RelayQueueController.cs` already has per-task-boundary checkpoints: pause
  is honored between tasks (lines ~208/223) and Sequential collects new tasks
  at each boundary (line ~271). The restart handoff belongs at this same
  boundary.
- Flagged tasks get a `NEEDS-REVIEW` marker under `.relay/<task>/` and
  queue collection already filters `!t.NeedsReview`
  (`RelayQueueController.PrivateHelpers.cs`, `CollectNewTasks`); completed
  tasks move to `llm-tasks/completed/`. A fresh drain therefore naturally
  runs only the remaining pending tasks — the continuation mechanism should
  lean on that rather than inventing a parallel queue snapshot.
- Launch path: the `./visual-relay` bootstrap execs the C# CLI
  (`tools/VisualRelay.Cli`) via `dotnet run`, so a source-checkout relaunch
  IS the recompile. Published (brew) installs exec a prebuilt binary — the
  protocol must still work there (restart without recompile, harmless).
- The app binds the loopback control API and **fails loud on bind conflict**
  (completed task `expose-instance-identity-and-fail-loud-on-bind-conflict`),
  so the replacement instance must not start until the old instance has fully
  exited. The litellm backend on `127.0.0.1:4000` is a separate process and
  survives restarts; the new instance reconnects to it.
- `RootPath` is not persisted anywhere today (the app opens on the launch
  directory) — the handoff must carry it explicitly or the restarted app will
  not be pointed at the repo the run was working on.

### What to build

1. **Protocol plumbing**: add `RunAllMode.RestartBetweenTasks`; it inherits
   Sequential semantics everywhere Sequential is special-cased (e.g.
   `skipPlanning`, boundary new-task collection).
2. **Drain behavior**: in this mode, after a task completes at the boundary
   checkpoint:
   - Task **sealed a commit** → write the handoff sidecar (see 3), stop the
     drain cleanly, and trigger the relaunch. The restart exists to load the
     new code; a task that committed nothing (flagged) changed no code, so
     **continue in-process to the next task instead of restarting** — this,
     plus the NEEDS-REVIEW skip, is the double guard against a flagged task
     causing a restart loop.
   - Restart after the final committed task too, so the session ends on the
     freshest build; the relaunched app then finds an empty pending queue and
     settles idle.
3. **Handoff + relaunch**: a sidecar (e.g. `.relay/restart-handoff.json`)
   recording rootPath, mode, drain id, timestamp, and the remaining pending
   count. Relaunch mechanics: spawn a detached relauncher that waits for the
   current process to exit (control-port bind conflict otherwise), then starts
   the app the same way it was started (source checkout → the recompiling
   path; published → the binary). On startup, when a fresh sidecar is present:
   reopen its rootPath, delete-or-mark the sidecar, and auto-continue Run All
   in RestartBetweenTasks mode. Guards: a stale sidecar (old timestamp, or
   rootPath missing) is discarded loudly, never auto-run; if a restart cycle
   completes zero tasks, end the run with a clear drain-log event instead of
   restarting again; a user pause always wins over auto-continue.
4. **Custom dropdown**: replace the plain ComboBox items with a two-line item
   template — protocol name, and beneath it one muted explanatory line for
   ALL three protocols (e.g. Standard: "Plan all tasks up front, then
   execute"; Sequential: "One task at a time, checking for new tasks between";
   Restart Between Tasks: "Sequential, plus the app rebuilds and relaunches
   after each committed task — for repos that build Visual Relay itself").
   Requirements: the collapsed control shows only the compact protocol name
   (two-line template must not bloat the closed state); the expanded popup is
   wide enough that "Restart Between Tasks" and every description render
   without truncation; description line uses the centralized theme
   colors/font sizes with accessible contrast in both themes, not a
   hard-coded gray; keyboard navigation and screen-reader naming
   (`AutomationProperties`) keep working; update the tooltip at
   `TopBar.axaml:124` to cover all three modes.
5. **Observability**: drain-summary events for the handoff
   (`restart-handoff`, with next pending task) and for startup continuation
   (`restart-resume`), each stamped with the running `version=…+sha` so logs
   prove the recompile happened; `/state` exposes the selected mode and a
   pending-handoff indicator so the control API can follow a restarting run.

### Constraints

- Repo-agnostic: the protocol must work pointed at any repository; nothing may
  assume the target repo is Visual Relay (self-hosting is the motivation, not
  a precondition).
- Standard and Sequential behavior must be byte-for-byte unchanged.
- No real-time sleeps in tests (TimeProvider patterns per
  `virtualize-watchdog-test-waits`); keep files under the 300-line guard.
- The relauncher must never leave two live instances or zero instances
  silently: bind-conflict remains fail-loud, and a failed relaunch (e.g. the
  new build does not start) must leave the sidecar plus a loud drain-log
  event for diagnosis rather than retry-looping.

### Tests (red first)

- Controller test: RestartBetweenTasks + a task that seals a commit → drain
  stops at the boundary with a handoff written; a flagged task → no handoff,
  drain proceeds to the next task in-process.
- Startup-continuation test: fresh sidecar + a queue containing one completed,
  one needs-review, and one pending task → run auto-continues with only the
  pending task, needs-review is skipped; stale sidecar → discarded, no
  auto-run.
- No-progress guard: a continuation cycle that completes zero tasks ends the
  run (no second handoff written).
- Headless UI test: dropdown popup contains all three items, each rendering
  name + description; the collapsed selection box shows the name only.

### Verification

- `./visual-relay check` fully green including the new tests.
- Manual self-hosted smoke: point at this repo, queue two trivial tasks, run
  with Restart Between Tasks, and confirm via drain logs that the second task
  ran under a different `version=…+sha` than the first.

Now I have a complete picture. Let me provide my diagnosis.

---

## Diagnosis

### The Problem

The drain log at `.relay/drain-20260716015038.log` confirms every task on 2026-07-15 executed under the same binary:
```
version=0.76+cfcc78dede9d3e3caa992ee60360c9a277a46b42
```
…even though tasks like `inject-timeprovider-into-product-retry-delays` committed `f72da68` and `fix-visual-relay-timing-bug` committed `6a49a41`. Those commits changed the source tree, but the running binary never picked them up because the drain runs the same process end-to-end.

### Root Cause

`RelayQueueController.DrainAsync()` at line 108 starts, processes every task in a single call, and returns only when the queue is empty, paused, or halted. There is no mechanism to stop mid-stream, recompile, and resume. The `RunAllMode` enum has only `Standard` (parallel planning) and `Sequential` (one-at-a-time), and both run in the same process.

### What Must Change (and Where)

**1. `RunAllMode` enum** — `src/VisualRelay.Core/Queue/RunAllMode.cs:7-14`
- Add `RestartBetweenTasks = 2` to the enum.
- This file is tiny; the new value plus its XML doc comment fit easily.

**2. `skipPlanning` assignment** — `src/VisualRelay.Core/Queue/RelayQueueController.cs:129`
- Today: `var skipPlanning = mode == RunAllMode.Sequential;`
- Must become: `var skipPlanning = mode is RunAllMode.Sequential or RunAllMode.RestartBetweenTasks;`
- This single-line change ensures RestartBetweenTasks skips parallel planning exactly like Sequential.

**3. Restart handoff at the per-task boundary** — `src/VisualRelay.Core/Queue/RelayQueueController.cs:271-281`
- Today lines 271-281 are the Sequential new-task collection checkpoint, inside `if (skipPlanning)`.
- In RestartBetweenTasks mode, after a task **seals a commit** (outcome.Status == Committed), the controller must:
  - Write `.relay/restart-handoff.json` with `rootPath`, `mode`, `drainId`, `timestamp`, `pendingCount` (remaining unprocessed tasks).
  - Write a `restart-handoff` event to the drain summary log (which `DrainSummaryLog.Write` at line 29 already stamps with `version=…+sha`).
  - Set state and return (stop the drain cleanly).
- If the task **flagged** (outcome.Status == Flagged), emit no handoff and continue to the next task in-process (the NEEDS-REVIEW skip on `CollectNewTasks` at line 90 provides the second guard).
- After the **final committed task**, still write the handoff so the session ends on the freshest build; the relaunched app will find an empty pending queue and settle idle.
- **No-progress guard**: if a restart cycle starts and zero tasks commit (all flagged or empty queue), the drain ends without writing a second handoff — a `restart-noprogress` drain-log event fires instead.
- This logic will go into a new partial class file (e.g. `RelayQueueController.RestartHandoff.cs`) to keep `RelayQueueController.cs` under its 300-line guard.

**4. `DrainAsync` return contract** — `src/VisualRelay.Core/Queue/RelayQueueController.cs`
- When RestartBetweenTasks stops mid-drain for a handoff, `State` must be set to a new value (e.g. `RelayQueueState.HandingOff` or a property on the controller) so the caller (`MainWindowViewModel.DrainQueueAsync`) can detect the handoff and trigger the relaunch.
- The `results` list must be returned as-is so the ViewModel still sees what happened.

**5. ViewModel relaunch handling** — `src/VisualRelay.App/ViewModels/MainWindowViewModel.Execution.cs:123-154`
- After `controller.DrainAsync()` returns in RestartBetweenTasks mode, if a restart handoff was written, the ViewModel must:
  - Spawn a detached relauncher process that waits for this process to exit, then launches the app the same way it started (the relauncher reads `Process.GetCurrentProcess().Id`, waits via `Process.GetProcessById().WaitForExit()`, then re-executes the launch command).
  - Signal the app to quit (`Environment.Exit(0)` or `desktop.Shutdown()`).
- The relauncher is a separate `.csproj` (`tools/VisualRelay.Relauncher/`) — a minimal console app that reads the handoff file, monitors the parent PID, waits for exit, then invokes the same bootstrap command.

**6. Startup handoff detection** — `src/VisualRelay.App/App.axaml.cs:29-82`
- After `viewModel.LoadInitialAsync()` (line 41), check for `.relay/restart-handoff.json`.
- If present and **fresh** (timestamp within a reasonable window, rootPath exists):
  - Reopen the app to the rootPath recorded in the sidecar.
  - Write `restart-resume` to the drain summary log (stamped with current `version=…+sha` — proving recompile).
  - Delete or rename the sidecar (to prevent double-resume).
  - Auto-continue Run All in RestartBetweenTasks mode.
- If **stale** (old timestamp, rootPath missing): discard with a loud log message, never auto-run.
- If **user has paused**: skip auto-continue (pause always wins).

**7. Dropdown UI** — `src/VisualRelay.App/Views/Controls/TopBar.axaml:119-124` + `MainWindowViewModel.Properties.cs:11-12`
- Replace the plain `ComboBox` with one that has an `ItemTemplate` producing two lines per expanded item: protocol name (bold) and muted description below.
- The `ComboBox.ItemTemplate` renders the two-line item; the `ComboBox` itself uses `SelectionBoxItemTemplate` or `DisplayMemberBinding` to show only the name when collapsed.
- Three protocol descriptions each fit on one muted line:
  - Standard: "Plan all tasks up front, then execute"
  - Sequential: "One task at a time, checking for new tasks between"
  - Restart Between Tasks: "Sequential, plus the app rebuilds and relaunches after each committed task"
- Description `TextBlock` uses the theme's `panelTitle` style (or inline `Foreground="#9AA3B1"` / `Foreground="{StaticResource ...}"`) for accessible contrast in both themes.
- `AutomationProperties.Name` on each item for screen-reader support.
- Update tooltip to cover all three modes.
- Popup `MinWidth` must be wide enough (~320px) for the longest description without truncation.

**8. `/state` endpoint** — `src/VisualRelay.App/Services/ControlApi.State.cs:18-69`
- Add `runAllMode` (enum name string) and `pendingHandoff` (bool) to the state JSON snapshot. `pendingHandoff` is true when `.relay/restart-handoff.json` exists and is fresh.

**9. Tests to add** (all new, under `tests/VisualRelay.Tests/`):

- **`RestartBetweenTasksControllerTests`**: 
  - Committed task → drain stops, handoff file written, handoff event in drain log.
  - Flagged task → no handoff, drain proceeds to next task in-process.
  - No-progress guard: cycle completes zero tasks → no second handoff, drain ends normally.

- **`RestartHandoffStartupTests`**:
  - Fresh sidecar + queue with 1 completed, 1 needs-review, 1 pending → auto-continue runs only the pending task (needs-review skipped via existing `CollectNewTasks` filter).
  - Stale sidecar → discarded, no auto-run.

- **`RestartBetweenTasksDropdownTests`** (headless UI):
  - Dropdown popup contains all three items with name + description.
  - Collapsed selection box shows name only.

- **`RunAllModesTests` updates**: 
  - `RunAllMode_HasStandardAndSequentialValues` must become `RunAllMode_HasAllThreeValues` and expect 3 values.

**10. 300-line guard**: `RelayQueueController.cs` is exactly 300 lines. The restart behavior will live in a new partial class file (`RelayQueueController.RestartHandoff.cs`), and the `DrainAsync` method only gains a few lines for the handoff check + the mode comparison change.

### Evidence Excerpts

1. **Drain log proves version never changed** — `.relay/drain-20260716015038.log` lines 1-13 all show `version=0.76+cfcc78dede9d3e3caa992ee60360c9a277a46b42` even after commits sealed by tasks.

2. **`DrainSummaryLog.Write` already stamps version** — `src/VisualRelay.Core/Logging/DrainSummaryLog.cs:29`: `line += $" version={Domain.VersionHelper.ReadInformationalVersion()}";` — the observability plumbing for `restart-handoff` and `restart-resume` events is already in place; new event types just call this existing method.

3. **Sequential boundary at lines 271-281** — `src/VisualRelay.Core/Queue/RelayQueueController.cs:271`: `if (skipPlanning) { SyncExternalTasks(); var newTasks = CollectNewTasks(Tasks, seenIds); ... }` — this is exactly where the restart handoff belongs (after task completion, within the skipPlanning guard, after new-task collection, before circuit breaker at line 283).

4. **`skipPlanning` at line 129** — `var skipPlanning = mode == RunAllMode.Sequential;` — must become a pattern match for both Sequential and RestartBetweenTasks.

5. **`CollectNewTasks` already filters `!t.NeedsReview`** — `RelayQueueController.PrivateHelpers.cs:90`: `tasks.Where(t => !t.NeedsReview && !seenIds.Contains(t.Id))` — the NEEDS-REVIEW skip for flagged tasks is already implemented; a fresh drain naturally runs only pending tasks.

6. **Theme colors** — `VisualRelayTheme.axaml:121-123`: `TextBlock.panelTitle` uses `Foreground="#9AA3B1"` and `FontSize="12"` — this is the centralized muted style the description line should use.

7. **`RunAllModesTests` expects exactly 2 values** — `tests/VisualRelay.Tests/RunAllModesTests.cs:21`: `Assert.Equal(2, values.Length);` — must become 3.

8. **Two-mode tooltip** — `TopBar.axaml:124`: `"Run All mode: Standard (parallel planning) or Sequential (one at a time)"` — must be updated.

9. **`RecordingTaskRunner` returns Committed with hash** — `tests/VisualRelay.Tests/TestDoubles.cs:217`: `new RelayTaskOutcome(taskId, RelayTaskOutcomeStatus.Committed, "hash", "commit", null)` — this will trigger the restart handoff in the controller test; `ScriptedOutcomeTaskRunner` can provide Flagged outcomes to test the skip path.

10. **`TestWaits.ForFileAsync` is event-driven** — `tests/VisualRelay.Tests/TestWaits.cs:13-57`: uses `FileSystemWatcher`, not polling — tests for the handoff sidecar can use this without real-time sleeps.

### Reproduction

```bash
# Point at this repo, queue two tasks, run with Restart Between Tasks (after change):
cd /path/to/visual-relay-repo
./visual-relay launch  # opens the app

# In the app: switch to "Restart Between Tasks" dropdown, click "Run All"
# Observe drain logs: the first task runs under one version+sha,
# the second task (after restart) runs under a different version+sha.

# Current (broken) behavior:
# All tasks in a drain run under the same version+sha, as shown in
# .relay/drain-20260716015038.log — every line has the identical version.
```
